title: How Many Times a Day: Extending -szor/-szer/-ször

sections.title: From three times onward
sections.content: In Unit 1 you learned egyszer, kétszer and háromszor by attaching -szor/-szer/-ször to a number, harmonizing the way most suffixes do. That rule is fully productive — it works on every number, not just the first three. Back vowels take -szor, front unrounded vowels take -szer, and front rounded vowels take -ször.

sections.title: How many times, four and up

items.english: How many times a day do you eat?

items.spanish: Napi négyszer eszem: reggelizem, ebédelek, uzsonnázom és vacsorázom.
items.english: I eat four times a day: breakfast, lunch, an afternoon snack, and dinner.

sections.content: hányszor pairs -szor with hány ("how many"), which you already know from asking prices and quantities — hány is a back-vowel word (that long á counts as back), so it keeps -szor even though most of the fronted-looking numbers around it take -szer. The rule is about the word's own vowels, not the ones near it.
